OSCILLATOR_CONFIGURATIONSOscillator Configurationsp. 48

OSCCONOSCILLATOR CONTROL REGISTERp. 50

offset 0xFD3 · 8 bits · reset 0b0110x000 · access R, R/W

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
7IDLENR/W0Chooses what a SLEEP instruction does: enter Idle mode or Sleep mode.
1Idle mode on SLEEP.
0Sleep mode on SLEEP.
6:4IRCFR/W0x6Picks the internal oscillator frequency; a change switches the clock frequency at once when the internal oscillator clocks the device. 111: HF-INTOSC, 16 MHz. 110: HF-INTOSC/2, 8 MHz (default). 101: HF-INTOSC/4, 4 MHz. 100: HF-INTOSC/8, 2 MHz. 011: HF-INTOSC/16, 1 MHz. With MFIOSEL (OSCCON2<0>) = 0: 010 HF-INTOSC/32, 500 kHz; 001 HF-INTOSC/64, 250 kHz; 000 LF-INTOSC, 31.25 kHz when INTSRC (OSCTUNE<7>) = 0, or HF-INTOSC/512, 31.25 kHz when INTSRC = 1. With MFIOSEL = 1: 010 MF-INTOSC, 500 kHz; 001 MF-INTOSC/2, 250 kHz; 000 LF-INTOSC, 31.25 kHz when INTSRC = 0, or MF-INTOSC/16, 31.25 kHz when INTSRC = 1. LF-INTOSC is the lowest-power internal choice.
3OSTSRxShows whether the Oscillator Start-up Timer has run out and the primary oscillator is running; its Reset state follows the IESO Configuration bit (CONFIG1H<7>).
1OST done; primary oscillator, set by FOSC<3:0>, running.
0OST still counting; primary oscillator not ready, device runs on HF-, MF- or LF-INTOSC.
2HFIOFSR0Shows whether the HF-INTOSC frequency has settled.
1Stable.
0Not yet stable.
1:0SCSR/W0x0Selects the system clock source; a change switches the clock source at once.
1xInternal oscillator block: HF-INTOSC, MF-INTOSC or LF-INTOSC.
01SOSC.
00Primary oscillator chosen by FOSC<3:0> (CONFIG1H<3:0>): OSC1/OSC2, or HF-INTOSC with or without the PLL.

OSCCON2OSCILLATOR CONTROL REGISTER 2p. 51

offset 0xFD2 · 8 bits · reset 0b000100x0 · access R, R/W

  • The figure on page 219 reads SOSCDRV 4 RW.
BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
6SOSCRUNR0Shows whether the system clock is running from the SOSC.
1System clock from the SOSC.
0System clock from another oscillator.
4SOSCDRVR/W1Forces the high-power SOSC circuit; does nothing when SOSC takes a digital clock input in place of a crystal.
1High-power SOSC circuit.
0Power level set by the SOSCSEL<1:0> Configuration bits.
3SOSCGOR/W0Keeps the SOSC running when nothing else asks for it.
1SOSC runs even when no source requests it.
0SOSC stops when no source requests it; no effect when the SOSC takes a digital clock input instead of a crystal.
1MFIOFSRxShows whether the MF-INTOSC frequency has settled.
1Stable.
0Not yet stable.
0MFIOSELR/W0Selects MF-INTOSC to supply the 500 kHz, 250 kHz and 31.25 kHz internal frequencies.
1MF-INTOSC replaces HF-INTOSC at 500 kHz, 250 kHz and 31.25 kHz.
0MF-INTOSC unused.

OSCTUNEOSCILLATOR TUNING REGISTERp. 52

offset 0xF9B · 8 bits · reset 0b00000000 · access R/W

  • TUN: the maker prints the codes listed; the codes between 011111 and 000001 and between 111111 and 100000 are shown as dots.
BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
7INTSRCR/W0Selects the source of the 31 kHz low-frequency device clock.
131.25 kHz from the 16 MHz HF-INTOSC divided by 512.
031 kHz from the LF-INTOSC oscillator.
6PLLENR/W0Turns the frequency multiplier PLL on or off.
1PLL on.
0PLL off.
5:0TUNR/W0x0Trims the fast RC oscillator (INTOSC) frequency: 011111 is the maximum, 000000 the calibrated center frequency, 100000 the minimum.
011111Highest frequency.
000001One step above center.
000000Center: the calibrated frequency.
111111One step below center.
100000Lowest frequency.

REFOCONREFERENCE OSCILLATOR CONTROL REGISTERp. 59

offset 0xF9A · 8 bits · reset 0b00000000 · access R/W

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
7ROONR/W0Puts the reference oscillator output on the REFO pin.
1Output on REFO.
0Output off.
5ROSSLPR/W0Chooses whether the reference oscillator keeps running during Sleep.
1Keeps running in Sleep.
0Stops in Sleep.
4ROSELR/W0Picks the reference clock's base clock; the primary oscillator is available only when FOSCx makes it the default, in Sleep or not.
1Primary oscillator (EC or HS).
0System clock, following any clock switch.
3:0RODIVR/W0x0Divides the base clock for the reference oscillator output, by 1 up to 32,768 in powers of two.
1111Base clock / 32,768.
1110Base clock / 16,384.
1101Base clock / 8,192.
1100Base clock / 4,096.
1011Base clock / 2,048.
1010Base clock / 1,024.
1001Base clock / 512.
1000Base clock / 256.
0111Base clock / 128.
0110Base clock / 64.
0101Base clock / 32.
0100Base clock / 16.
0011Base clock / 8.
0010Base clock / 4.
0001Base clock / 2.
0000Base clock, undivided.

RESETResetp. 75

RCONRESET CONTROL REGISTERp. 76

offset 0xFD0 · 8 bits · reset 0b01111100 · access R, R/W

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
7IPENR/W0Turns on high and low priority levels for interrupts.
1Priority levels on.
0Priority levels off (PIC16CXXX Compatibility mode).
6SBORENR/W1Turns the BOR on or off from software when BOREN<1:0> = 01: 1 on, 0 off. With BOREN<1:0> = 00, 10 or 11 the bit is disabled and reads 0.
5CM#R/W1Flags a Configuration Mismatch Reset; cleared by the Reset, set again by software.
1No Configuration Mismatch Reset.
0Configuration Mismatch Reset happened; software sets the bit again after it.
4RI#R/W1Flags a Reset caused by the RESET instruction; cleared by the Reset, set only by firmware.
1No RESET instruction executed; set only by firmware.
0A RESET instruction reset the device; software sets the bit again after a Brown-out Reset.
3TO#R1Flags a Watchdog Timer time-out.
1Set by power-up, CLRWDT or SLEEP.
0WDT time-out happened.
2PD#R1Flags that a SLEEP instruction has run since power-up or the last CLRWDT.
1Set by power-up or CLRWDT.
0Cleared by a SLEEP instruction.
1POR#R/W0Flags a Power-on Reset; cleared by the Reset, set only by firmware. BOR# = 0 with POR# = 1 marks a Brown-out Reset, provided software set POR# to 1 right after the Power-on Reset.
1No Power-on Reset; set only by firmware.
0Power-on Reset happened; software sets the bit again after it.
0BOR#R/W0Flags a Brown-out Reset; cleared by the Reset, set only by firmware.
1No Brown-out Reset; set only by firmware.
0Brown-out Reset happened; software sets the bit again after it.

offset 0xFFC · 8 bits · reset 0b00000000 · access R/C, R/W

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
7STKFULR/C0Flags a full or overflowed stack; cleared by user software or a POR.
1Stack full or overflowed.
0Not full, no overflow.
6STKUNFR/C0Flags a stack underflow; cleared by user software or a POR.
1Underflow happened.
0No underflow.

STATUSSTATUS REGISTERp. 118

offset 0xFD8 · 8 bits · reset 0b000xxxxx · access R/W

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
4NR/WxSet when a signed (two's complement) result is negative, copying the ALU result's MSB.
1Negative.
0Positive.
3OVR/WxSet when a signed (two's complement) operation overflows the 7-bit magnitude and flips the sign bit, bit 7.
1Signed overflow in this operation.
0No overflow.
2ZR/WxSet when an arithmetic or logic result is zero.
1Result zero.
0Result not zero.
1DCR/WxFor ADDWF, ADDLW, SUBLW and SUBWF: 1 when the result's fourth low-order bit carried out, 0 when not. For a borrow the sense is inverted; subtraction adds the two's complement of the second operand.
0CR/WxFor ADDWF, ADDLW, SUBLW and SUBWF: 1 when the result's most significant bit carried out, 0 when not. For a borrow the sense is inverted; subtraction adds the two's complement of the second operand.

FLASH_PROGRAM_MEMORYFlash Program Memoryp. 125

EECON1EEPROM CONTROL REGISTER 1p. 127

offset 0xF7F · 8 bits · reset 0bxx00x000 · access R/S, R/W

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
7EEPGDR/WxChooses whether an access goes to Flash program memory or to data EEPROM.
1Flash program memory.
0Data EEPROM.
6CFGSR/WxChooses between the Configuration registers and the Flash program or data EEPROM memory.
1Configuration registers.
0Flash program memory or data EEPROM.
4FREER/W0Turns the next WR command into an erase of the program memory row TBLPTR points to.
1Next WR erases the row at TBLPTR; the bit clears when the erase finishes.
0Write only.
3WRERRR/WxSet when a write ends early, from a Reset during self-timed programming or an improper write attempt; EEPGD and CFGS are left as they were so the failure can be traced.
1Write ended early.
0Write finished.
2WRENR/W0Permits or blocks write cycles to Flash program memory and data EEPROM.
1Write cycles allowed.
0Write cycles blocked.
1WRR/S0Starts a self-timed erase or write; software can only set it, and hardware clears it when the write is done.
1Starts a data EEPROM erase/write, or a program memory erase or write; self-timed, cleared by hardware at completion, cannot be cleared by software.
0The EEPROM write cycle has finished.
0RDR/S0Starts a one-cycle EEPROM read; software can only set it, hardware clears it, and it cannot be set while EEPGD = 1 or CFGS = 1.
1Starts an EEPROM read, which takes one cycle; cleared by hardware, cannot be cleared by software, cannot be set when EEPGD = 1 or CFGS = 1.
0No read started.

7MDENR/W0Turns the modulator on; while off it gives no output.

1Inverted.
0Not inverted.

0MDBITR/W0Lets software drive the modulation source by hand; it works only when MDSRC selects MDBIT as the source.

7WCOLwhen I2CR/W0Write collision flag. As master transmitter, 1 means SSPBUF was written when I2C conditions did not allow a transmission to start; as slave transmitter, 1 means SSPBUF was written while the previous word was still going out. 0 means no collision. Software clears it. Ignored while receiving.
7WCOLwhen SPIR/W0Write collision flag.

6SSPOVR/W0Receive overflow flag. As SPI slave, 1 means a byte arrived while SSPBUF still held the last one, and the byte in SSPSR is lost; overflow happens only in slave mode, and SSPBUF must be read even when only sending to keep it from setting. In I2C receive, 1 means a byte arrived while SSPBUF still held the last one; ignored in transmit. 0 means no overflow. Software clears it. In I2C, with the port enabled, SDA and SCL must be set as inputs.

RXB0CONRECEIVE BUFFER 0 CONTROL REGISTERp. 397

offset 0xF60 · 8 bits · reset 0b00000000 · access R, R/C, R/W

  • The bit row prints FILHITF4; the bit's description prints FILHIT.
  • The bit row prints RXB0DBEN; the bit's description prints RB0DBEN.
  • FILHIT0: the maker prints the codes listed; the codes between 01110 and 00000 are shown as dots.
BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
7RXFULR/C0Set by the CAN module when a message arrives; software clears it after reading the buffer. While it is set the buffer counts as full and no new message is loaded into it. RXB0IF in PIR5 can be cleared after RXFUL is cleared; if RXB0IF is cleared while RXFUL stays set, RXB0IF sets again.
1Buffer holds a received message.
0Buffer is free for a new message.
6RXM1R/W0Receive buffer mode. Modes 1 and 2: one bit choosing whether the acceptance filters apply. Mode 0: high bit of RXM<1:0>, with RXM0 in bit 5: 11 takes every message, errors included, ignoring the filters; 10 only valid extended-identifier messages, EXIDEN in RXFnSIDL at 1; 01 only valid standard-identifier messages, EXIDEN at 0; 00 all valid messages as EXIDEN in RXFnSIDL decides.
1Every message, errors included; acceptance filters ignored.
when Mode 1, 2
0Valid messages that pass the acceptance filters.
when Mode 1, 2
5RXM0when Mode 0R/W0Mode 0: low bit of RXM<1:0>, read with RXM1 in bit 6 to choose which messages the buffer takes.
5RTRROwhen Mode 1, 2R0Modes 1 and 2, read-only: set when the received message is a remote transmission request.
1Remote transmission request received.
0No remote transmission request received.
4FILHITF4when Mode 1, 2R0Modes 1 and 2: bit 4 of FILHIT<4:0>, the number of the acceptance filter that took the message.
3RXRTRROwhen Mode 0R0Mode 0, read-only: set when the received message is a remote transmission request.
1Remote transmission request received.
0No remote transmission request received.
3FILHIT3when Mode 1, 2R0Modes 1 and 2: bit 3 of FILHIT<4:0>, the number of the acceptance filter that took the message.
2RXB0DBENwhen Mode 0R/W0Mode 0: double buffering. When set, a message that overflows Receive Buffer 0 is written into Receive Buffer 1.
1Receive Buffer 0 overflows into Receive Buffer 1.
0Receive Buffer 0 does not overflow into Receive Buffer 1.
2FILHIT2when Mode 1, 2R0Modes 1 and 2: bit 2 of FILHIT<4:0>, the number of the acceptance filter that took the message.
1JTOFFwhen Mode 0R0Mode 0: jump table offset, a read-only copy of RXB0DBEN, so RXB0CON and RXB1CON can share one filter jump table.
1Jump table offset between 6 and 7.
0Jump table offset between 1 and 0.
1FILHIT1when Mode 1, 2R0Modes 1 and 2: bit 1 of FILHIT<4:0>, the number of the acceptance filter that took the message.
0FILHIT0R0Filter hit bit 0. Mode 0: which acceptance filter let the message into Receive Buffer 0. Modes 1 and 2: bit 0 of FILHIT<4:0>, which with FILHIT<4:1> numbers the acceptance filter that let the message into this buffer, 00000 for RXF0 up to 01111 for RXF15.
1RXF1 (Mode 0).
when Mode 0
0RXF0 (Mode 0).
when Mode 0

B5CONTX/RX BUFFER ‘n’ CONTROL REGISTERS INp. 404

offset 0xED0 · 8 bits · reset 0b00000000 · access R, R/W

  • FILHIT: the maker prints the codes listed; the codes between 01110 and 00001 are shown as dots.
  • Available in Mode 1 and 2 only.
BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
7RXFULwhen RECEIVER/W0Set by the CAN module when a message arrives; software clears it after reading the buffer. While it is set the buffer counts as full and no new message is loaded into it.
1Buffer holds a received message.
0Buffer is free for a new message.
7TXBIFwhen TRANSMITR/W0Transmit mode: set when the buffer has sent a message successfully. Cleared automatically when TXREQ is set.
1Message sent successfully.
0No message sent.
6RXM1when RECEIVER/W0Receive mode: chooses which messages the buffer takes.
1Every message, partial and invalid ones included; acceptance filters ignored.
0Valid messages that pass the acceptance filters.
6TXABTwhen TRANSMITR0Transmit mode: set when the message was aborted. Cleared automatically when TXREQ is set.
1Aborted.
0Not aborted.
5RXRTRROwhen RECEIVER0Receive mode, read-only: set when the received message is a remote transmission request.
1Remote transmission request received.
0Not a remote transmission request.
5TXLARBwhen TRANSMITR0Transmit mode: set when the message lost arbitration while it was being sent. Cleared automatically when TXREQ is set.
1Arbitration lost during sending.
0Arbitration not lost during sending.
4:0FILHITwhen RECEIVER0x0Receive mode: number of the acceptance filter that let the last message into this buffer.
01111Filter RXF15.
01110Filter RXF14.
00001Filter RXF1.
00000Filter RXF0.
4TXERRwhen TRANSMITR0Transmit mode: set when a bus error happened while the message was being sent. Cleared automatically when TXREQ is set.
1Bus error during sending.
0No bus error during sending.
3TXREQwhen TRANSMITR/W0Set to ask for the buffer's message to be sent, which also clears TXABT, TXLARB and TXERR; hardware clears it once the message has gone. Clearing it in software while set asks for the message to be aborted. While it is set, or a transmission is under way, the transmit buffer registers are read-only.
1Send requested; TXABT, TXLARB and TXERR cleared.
0Cleared by hardware once the message is sent.
2RTRENwhen TRANSMITR/W0Transmit mode: automatic answer to remote frames. When set, a received remote transmission request sets TXREQ by itself.
1A received remote transmission request sets TXREQ.
0A received remote transmission request leaves TXREQ alone.
1:0TXPRIwhen TRANSMITR/W0x0Transmit priority: the order in which the transmit buffers are sent. The CAN message identifier is not changed.
11Level 3, the highest.
10Level 2.
01Level 1.
00Level 0, the lowest.

offset 0xE70 · 8 bits · reset 0b00000000 · access R/W

4:0FLCR/W0x0Filter length count: how many data bits the standard data byte filter compares. Mode 0: not used, forced to 00000. Codes 00000 to 10010 give 0 to 18 bits; how many are compared depends on DLC<3:0> of the incoming message (RXBnDLC<3:0>, or BnDLC<3:0> for a buffer set as receiver): DLC 0000 compares none; 0001 up to 8 bits of RXFnEID<7:0>, set by FLC<2:0>; 0010 up to 16 bits of RXFnEID<15:0>, set by FLC<3:0>; 0011 up to 18 bits of RXFnEID<17:0>, set by FLC<4:0>; each against as many data bits of the message.
00000-100100 to 18 bits for the standard data byte filter; the number used depends on the message's DLC<3:0>.
